From: network-team@halcyonhealth.com
To: david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Outbound controls for private endpoints — evidence request

Hi David,

Thanks for the walkthrough today. Halcyon's network and security teams need a concise artefact so our perimeter team can sign off:

- canonical list of egress IP(s) used by Redwood private runtime when deployed in our VPC (or clear guidance on when IPs can be ephemeral).
- DNS behavior for outbound calls (do you rely on SNI-only routing? split-horizon DNS? FQDNs expected).
- TLS termination model (does Redwood terminate TLS inside customer VPC, or is there a control-plane mTLS hop?).
- expected ports and any long-lived TCP connections we should permit.
- recommended firewall policy snippet we can paste into our perimeter ruleset.

Could you produce a short "PKI + IP provenance" manifest and any sample iptables/firewall snippet? We also prefer an evidence bundle (tcpdump/sample cert fingerprints) to attach to our audit.

I've attached a csv where we captured the first-pass IPs from our PoC traffic — we may need confirmation or corrections.

Appreciate a scoped response by EOD Friday so we can make the change window.

— Sam (Halcyon network)
[Attachment: egress-ip-proposal.csv (text/csv, 4 KB)]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, network-team@halcyonhealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Outbound controls for private endpoints — evidence request

Hi all —

Attaching the first draft of the manifest here (inline highlights + attached reference stubs). High level summary first:

- Egress origins: For private deployments in customer VPCs, outbound connections are by default sourced from the customer's NAT (i.e., Redwood processes run on customer subnets). However, when customers opt into Redwood-managed NAT for simpler ops (rare), outbound will come from a small set of static NAT IPs we operate — see table below.

STATIC NAT POOL (Redwood-managed, only when requested):
- 3 IPv4 addresses: 35.189.12.40, 35.189.12.41, 35.189.12.42
- Rotation policy: address reassignment only during major infra upgrades; we notify customers 30 days in advance.

EPHEMERAL BEHAVIOR (default customer-managed):
- Default: outbound flows egress via the VPC's NAT gateway(s). Customers must map egress expectations to their NAT design (elastic IPs, NAT gateways, or firewall SNAT).
- If private runtime uses ephemeral worker instances (autoscaling), source ports and source IPs are determined by your VPC NAT.

DNS & SNI guidance:
- We recommend allowlisting by FQDN where possible: *.redwood-inference.com (control plane), runtime-callouts.redwood-inference.com (service discovery), and (for model pulls) models.redwood-inference.net.
- If you use split-horizon DNS internally, ensure resolvers for runtime-hosted machines can resolve the external FQDNs — use conditional forwarding if needed.
- SNI: we include SNI in TLS handshakes; do not rely on SNI alone for firewalling — allow at the IP or FQDN level.

TLS / PKI:
- Control-plane calls are mTLS authenticated for dedicated/private pilots where configured. For standard private deployments, outbound from runtime to public services uses TLS with Redwood client certs only when explicitly configured.
- Certificate thumbprints (SHA256) for control-plane endpoints:
  - CN=control.redwood-inference.com — SHA256: 3a:5b:...:9f (fingerprint redacted here).
- We will provide full truncated fingerprints in the evidence bundle.

Ports and long-lived connections:
- Outbound: 443 (HTTPS) is primary.
- If you enable telemetry streaming, we may establish long-lived TLS connections over 443 (keepalive). Allow stateful inspection to avoid premature timeouts.

Recommended firewall snippet (pasteable):
- Allow TCP 443 to models.redwood-inference.net (resolved IPs listed in the attachment)
- Allow outbound to control.redwood-inference.com (443) and runtime-callouts.redwood-inference.com (443)

We have produced a small evidence pack and a short SOP for iptables/NACL examples — attaching both.

Laura
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: private-endpoint-egress-sop.md (text/markdown, 6 KB)]

Thanks Laura — that helps a lot. Quick clarifications from our side before we start firewall changes:

- Can you confirm whether the three static addresses are reachable from our VPC without any additional routing (i.e., they're public internet addresses we will allow outbound to)?
- For the mTLS option: who holds the client certs (Redwood or Halcyon) in the managed-mTLS configuration? We need that for our CSR and key custody notes.
- Please confirm the expected DNS names we should allow for model fetches; we prefer explicit hostnames rather than wildcard rules.

Our auditor also requested a short pcap sample showing a complete TLS handshake with SNI and the server cert fingerprint. Could you add that to the evidence bundle? If possible, also include a minimal iptables snippet that maps to an AWS NACL example.

— Priya (Halcyon sec-ops)

From: david_kim@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Private endpoints — outbound provenance, DNS split-horizon & PKI manifest

Priya / team —

Short answers inline and bundle links below. Full artifacts are attached and uploaded to the Drive link in the header.

- Static addresses: yes — the three IPv4 addresses listed are public egress NATs we operate when customers opt in to Redwood-managed NAT. They are reachable over the public internet and should be allowlisted as destination IPs in your outbound firewall.

- Managed mTLS model: when Redwood operates the termination (managed mode) we hold the client certs and rotate them on a 90-day cadence; when the customer requests mutual-auth on their side we provide a CSR template and public CA chain and the customer manages the private keys. We'll state the custody model clearly in the final SOP.

- Explicit hostnames for model pulls (no wildcard recommendation):
  - models-1.us.redwood-inference.net
  - models-2.us.redwood-inference.net
  - artifacts.redwood-inference.net

Evidence bundle includes: truncated pcap (tls-handshake-sample.pcap), cert fingerprints (text), and small AWS NACL / iptables examples.

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.internal/h/egress-proof/halcyon-2026 (read-only; expiration 2026-12-01)

I've attached the final evidence zip and the SOP. Please confirm when your firewall team completes the control change window and we'll run an end-to-end check from our side.

Thanks —
David
Product Security, Redwood Inference
